summary: Theorems4.1 and4.6 fail under their general printed hypotheses. P4 andP5 are Major invalid derivations on the Kan and main Hurewicz proof paths with analytically supported repairs. P3 is a Minor coefficient-domain defect whose inspected application already uses the correct ambient system. No counterexample to the GM main theorem, normal Thom-Mather application, Kan conclusion or Hurewicz conclusion is asserted.

problems.title: Van Kampen needs allowable-path connectivity

source_claim.claim: Ordinary path connectivity of U0,U1 and their intersection suffices for surjectivity and kernel description of perverse fundamental groups.

assumptions: Open cover U0,U1 with ordinary path-connected members and intersection

counterexample.space: R² with closed vertical segment S, endpoints 0-strata, interior 1-stratum; CS, nonnormal permitted
counterexample.perversity: p=-2 on segment interior, p=-1 endpoints, so Dp=1
counterexample.cover: U0 removes closed upward ray from y=1/2, U1 removes closed downward ray from y=-1/2
counterexample.hypothesis_verification: Both sets and intersection ordinary pathconnected through middle gap; cover all R²; basepoint(1,0)
counterexample.proof: Two-skeleta avoid S. Both Uireg slit planes simplyconnected; Xreg radial deformation retract onto radius2 circle. Full analytic proof in reportSection2 and root_van_kampen_counterexample.json.

counterevidence: Normal Thom-Mather application Cor4.2 supplies regular connectivity through Remark1.6.
This nonnormal example does not refute that application.
problems.impact: Actual conclusion of a substantive named Van Kampen theorem fails under printed assumptions.

correction.statement: For CS sets require path-connected regular parts of U0,U1,U0 intersection U1.
correction.verification_status: Supported by allowable connecting paths and finite-subdivision argument; broader groupoid generalization not claimed

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: The segment-stratified R2 is a CS set allowed by Theorem4.1; p=-2 on its codimension1 middle and p=-1 at endpoints gives Dp=1. With the two complementary rays removed, both open sets and their intersection are ordinary path-connected; regular parts of each open are simply connected slit planes, whereas regular X retracts onto a circle. All 1/2-simplices avoid the singular set, so the asserted map is1*1->Z and is not onto.
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: Normality is not assumed in this theorem; the later normal Thom-Mather application has stronger regular-part connectivity and is not refuted.
independent_verification.repair_check: Require regular-part path connectivity of the opens and overlap, with suitable CS finiteness for subdivision; no broader groupoid theorem is claimed.

problems.title: Unrestricted codimensional perversities are incompatible with coarsening

source_claim.claim: For codimensional p<=t a coarsening with no exceptional strata induces isomorphisms of pi0p and pi1p.

counterexample.space: Y singular z-axis; X refines it into origin and two open rays; same regular part
counterexample.perversity: p2=-1,p3=1; Dp2=1,Dp3=0; finite values and p<=t
counterexample.hypothesis_verification: Conical origin link S² with two poles; other singular links circles. All CS conditions, no codim1 strata, no exceptional strata.
counterexample.claimed_result: pi1p(X) isomorphic to pi1p(Y) via identity
counterexample.correct_result: pi1p(X)=1, pi1p(Y)=Z; identity not Gajer simplicial map
counterexample.proof: Y two-skeleton avoidsaxis; X transverse meridian triangle meets only origin at one interiorpoint (bound0), boundary avoidsaxis; killsgenerator. Image inY violates bound-1. Nu*Dp(origin)=1>0=Dp(origin).

counterevidence: Proposition2.5 already states the required functorial inequality.
problems.impact: False central fundamental-group invariance assertion in the claimed broader range; GM main theorem not refuted.

correction.statement: Restrict to GM perversities (and no codim1 strata); then complementary perversity monotonicity gives nu*Dp<=Dp.
correction.verification_status: Supported relative to checked source-stratum argument; no strongest general range claimed

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: Refine the axis stratum of R3 by its origin and two open rays. No stratum becomes regular; both stratifications are CS. The same codimensional p2=-1,p3=1 obeys p<=t but has Dp2=1,Dp3=0. Coarse 1/2-simplices avoid the axis, giving Z. In the refinement a transverse meridian bounds a p-full disk meeting only the origin in a simplex interior, killing its generator and giving trivial pi1. That disk is not coarse-p-full, so even the proposed induced simplicial map fails.
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: This is not a GM perversity and does not refute TheoremA/5.1. The source's later reference to GM does not impose it on the broader statement.
independent_verification.repair_check: For GM, nondecreasing complementary perversity yields the functorial inequality. Using a coarse conical chart and the common regular part, the source-stratum radial filling supplies the required injectivity with subdivision; retain this supported restricted repair, not an unrestricted coarsening theorem.

problems.title: Local coefficients must be defined on the larger member of the cone pair

source_claim.claim: Relative cone homology is defined and vanishes for every local system E on GpL.

assumptions: Rank-one integral local system on GpL with monodromy-1

counterexample.claimed_result: Relative group with this E is defined
counterexample.correct_result: Sign local system cannot extend to simplyconnected Gajercone
counterexample.proof: Cone meridian is p-full-nullhomotopic; any ambient local system restricts with trivial monodromy.

counterevidence: Proposition5.2 takes system on larger space already.
problems.impact: Invalid coefficient-domain quantifier, inspected downstream use preserved.

correction.statement: Take E on GpconeL and restrict it to GpL; common low skeleta give vanishing.

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: For L=S1 and apex Dp=0, a sign-monodromy integral local system on GpL cannot extend over the simply connected Gajer cone. Thus the relative group using it on the larger cone is undefined under the arbitrary-link-system quantifier.
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: Proposition5.2 already starts with a local system on the larger space, so its inspected use has the needed premise.
independent_verification.repair_check: State the system on Gp(cL) and restrict to GpL.

problems.title: The specified radial horn projection is not continuous

source_claim.claim: Radial projection from missing face barycentre defines an affine whole-simplex horn retraction.

assumptions: Trivially stratified target horn; all continuous simplices allowable

counterexample.correct_result: Undefined centre; approaching along different rays gives distinct limits
counterexample.proof: Two fixed endpoint images along radial rays contradict continuity at their common starting midpoint.

counterevidence: Kan conclusion is true with explicit PL replacement.
No counterexample to Gajer existence asserted.
problems.impact: The discontinuous specified map invalidates the Kan proof in Proposition2.3 (p8). Page12 uses Kan to represent homotopy classes and homotopies by individual p-full simplices, including in Proposition3.5. This is a Major invalid derivation on a foundational proof path. The explicit PL repair restores the conclusion without validating the original construction.

correction.statement: m=min_{i!=k}t_i; rho_i=t_i-m(i!=k),rho_k=t_k+ell*m. Missing-face inverse t_i=y_i+y_k/ell,t_k=0; other faces fixed.
correction.verification_status: Continuity, retraction, piecewise linear fibres and allowability bounds analytically verified

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: The actual source's radial projection from the missing face barycentre is undefined there and has different limiting images along rays toward distinct horn points. In dimension2 it cannot continuously extend and is not affine. This invalidates the printed Kan construction used for simplex representatives of intersection homotopy classes.
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: The failure is in the proof, not Kan's truth. The explicit piecewise-linear formula rho_i=t_i-m (i!=k), rho_k=t_k+ell*m with m=min_{i!=k}t_i fixes the horn, has ambient fibres of dimension<=1 and missing-face fibres dimension0.
independent_verification.repair_check: The displayed inverse on the missing face t_i=y_i+y_k/ell proves its homeomorphism onto the horn; finite piecewise-linear fibre bounds supply allowability. This repairs the core construction without downgrading the original failure.

problems.title: The conical product family is not a basis

source_claim.claim: C×ctL and C×L×(a,b) form a basis of all open subsets of the chart.

assumptions: LinkS2 is simplyconnected, satisfying theorem link hypothesis

counterexample.claimed_result: Every open set is union of listed products
counterexample.correct_result: Nonempty proper angular sector O×(a,b) contains no such angular-saturated basis set
counterexample.proof: Every listed set contains entire L at every occupied radius.

counterevidence: Depth induction applies to all open subsets away from centralstratum.
problems.impact: The false basis claim fails to establish Pk for arbitrary chart opens, particularly W intersection V in the maximal-open step on p26. Theorem6.4 is then used on that page to prove main Theorem6.1(2), equivalently TheoremB(ii). This is a Major core proof gap; depth induction supplies a supported repair, not a counterexample to the Hurewicz conclusion.

correction.statement: Add all opens off centralstratum to tipproduct neighborhoods; intersections have Pk by smaller depth or conelemma; finite unions and directedcompact-chain limits complete proof.

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: On the cone over S2 with k2 and apex p0, the link satisfies the theorem's connectivity hypothesis. A proper off-apex angular sector contains no angularly saturated proposed basis element. Thus arbitrary W intersect V in the maximal-open step is not covered by the claimed basis argument; Theorem6.4 is explicitly used for main Theorem6.1(2)/B(ii).
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: This is a false basis assertion and missing core proof step, not a Hurewicz counterexample.
independent_verification.repair_check: Add all opens off the central stratum, of smaller depth, and tip-product neighborhoods. Depth induction, finite intersections/unions and compactness of finite chains justify directed unions and the subsequent Zorn step.
